segments.text: This is the debrief for Independent QC, where you double-program a demographics table and report every disagreement with production. First, build an independent QC table from the specification. Second, compare it with production cell by cell, using a tolerance. Third, report one row per discrepancy, and none when the tables agree.

segments.text: The QC function finds the arms from the data, instead of assuming their names. For each arm, it takes that arm's subjects only. Then it computes n, the mean age, and its standard deviation. Percent female divides by the subjects in that arm, which is exactly where production went wrong.

visual.title: Built from the spec, not from production

segments.text: Compare tables looks at every column the two tables share, except arm. It starts from an empty data frame with the report's columns, so a clean comparison returns zero rows of the right shape. Then it walks every arm and every column, cell by cell. A difference counts only when it exceeds the tolerance, so floating point noise is never reported.

segments.text: Three mistakes account for most failed attempts. Comparing with double equals flags differences that are only rounding noise, and the tolerance check fails. Checking only the column you know is wrong misses discrepancies in a different production table. And returning null when everything matches, instead of an empty data frame, fails the clean check.
